highlights: Review proposed file changes in the app: browse them, read feedback, edit comments, and ask the agent about specific changed lines.
A redesigned sidebar keeps tasks organized, lets you reorder pinned tasks, and helps you find tasks and project files faster.
Attach general files and images more easily, preview images and videos, and save unfinished prompts with their attachments for later.
New plugins connect to UC San Diego Kuali Build and n8n, using your own sign-in or API key and only the permissions you authorize.
Opt-in computer use lets the app work on your desktop with visible setup and activity, and updates install more reliably.
You can now download and install app updates from inside the app, with progress, release notes, and an automatic restart.
Each model now uses the correct account key, and you can replace or remove keys without restarting the app.
Signing in to add-ons such as GitHub, Google Workspace, and Microsoft 365 is easier and more flexible.
When the app asks you to approve work, you now see complete details, including full proposed file changes.
Many small fixes make the app more stable and polished, including a refreshed look and better voice input on Mac.
Memory now turns on by default, can backfill seven days of past work, and can sync your notes between computers through OneDrive.
Cloud models were refreshed, adding GPT-6.1 Sol, and Flash is now the default model for new chats.
The managed Codex engine now updates itself automatically after startup when no Codex session is running, with clearer handling when the shared engine is already updated.
Integration tool rejections now explain how to recover, and credentials stay fresh while the app is idle.
Threads now use Done and Reopen wording, and Windows computer use no longer opens an extra console window.

setup: Check for app updates under Settings, About, Check for Updates. A Harness update also carries UCSD-managed configuration, built-in skills, and the managed plugin composition.

The managed Codex engine updates in the background after starting unless a Codex session is running; if that attempt is skipped or fails, use the provider update action in the sidebar or provider settings.
faq: Computer use is off by default. Turn it on under Settings, General, Computer use; on macOS it requests Accessibility and Screen Recording access before the driver starts.
Permission modes are set per thread. New threads start in Full access unless you choose otherwise, and changing the mode in one thread does not affect any other thread.
privacy: Memory is on by default and keeps daily summaries of your threads as local notes on each machine. You can turn it off under Settings, General, Memory; your existing notes stay.
OneDrive sync is optional and separate from local notes. When enabled, notes are copied to your OneDrive and shared between your computers; signing out stops sync and keeps the notes.
skills: TritonAI Commons is the public skill library in Settings, Skills. AI Team and Community skills come from Commons; skills you create or add locally stay under Your Skills until you publish them.
citizen: To share a local skill with UCSD, select Share with UCSD under Your Skills and accept the public-share confirmation. Submission opens a ready-for-review pull request; Harness never merges it.
Only submit material that is safe to publish. Do not include secrets, private data, internal infrastructure details, or files you lack permission to share.
models: Harness remembers your provider, model, and model options for new threads. A project's configured model takes precedence over that remembered selection.
Your TritonAI access key is managed under Settings, Runtime. Change key verifies access and restarts the local runtime; changing one connection keeps the other connection's key.
